To burn Incense on the Golden Altar before the Ark: the Priests took a Censer, and filled it with Fire from the Altar of Burnt Sacrifice, and then came to the Altar of Incense before the Vail, and there put the Incense on the Fire in the Censer; during the evaporating of which, the People in the Court were pouring out their Prayers for Pardon, each per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son by himself, see <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.1, to 7, 8, 9, 34, 35, 36. and 40.26, 27. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 1.9, 10. Even all the Ordinances of Worship commanded by God, did the Priests perform in it; all which Services in the Holy Place, do but typifie the true Services in the Gospel-Church, of all made Priests by the Blood of Christ, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet,</ns0:hi> 2.5, 9. and <ns0:hi>Revel.</ns0:hi> 1.5, 6. and 5.9, 10. Offering Prayers and Praises to God continually in the Name of Christ, perfu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med with the Incense of his Merits, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 1.11. compare <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 8.3. obtaining thereby the light of his Grace through his Spirit, and the Bread of Life, till they are perfected by their great High-Priest, and carried into the Holy of Holiest, there to be praising and enjoying God in him for ever, as he hath prayed for them, and promised to them, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.2, 3. and 17.20, 21.</ns0:note> accomplishing the service <ns0:hi>of God.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 But into the second <ns0:hi>went</ns0:hi> the High-Priest alone once every year <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">This Verse contains the special Anniversary of the High-Priest alone in the inward Tabernacle the <ns0:hi>Holy of Holiest,</ns0:hi> of which you have the Law, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.14. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.2, &c. Into this Place the High-Priest was to enter once a Year only, and every year to repeat it, as <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.10. upon the Atonement-day being the tenth day of the month <ns0:hi>Tisri,</ns0:hi> the seventh month in their Ecclesiastical year, and the first of their Civil; that day was he to enter several times into that Place, first for Himself, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.11, 12, 13, 14. and then for the People, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 15, 16, &c. carrying in the Blood first within the Vail, and then coming out again, and car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rying in the Incense on the Golden Censer; none of the other Priests were to enter into the Holy Place while he was ministring, but him alone, as <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.17.</ns0:note>, not without blood <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">When he first entred into the Holiest of all, it was with the Blood of a young Bull, of a Ram, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.3, 14. with the Blood of the He-Goat, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15, 27. After he had offered the Incense on his Golden Censer, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. he must sprinkle the Blood upon the Mercy-Seat and before it, by which expia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tory Blood there was made an Atonement, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12, 13, 14.</ns0:note>, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">First, for his sinful Self and Family, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. and then for the Ignorances, Incogitancies, Errors, and all sorts of Sins committed by the People, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 7.27. all of them being committed with some error of the Understanding, which Type in all its parts, was perfectly fulfilled in Christ the Gospel-High-Priest, as is shewn in the following Ver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses, whereby not only his Office, but his Services are tran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scendently set above, and preferred to all the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> ones.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 The Holy Ghost <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">God the Spirit himself, the third Relation in the Deity, the Author of all the <ns0:hi>Mosaical</ns0:hi> Institutions, who command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed all these ritual Ceremonial Services in this Tabernacle to be performed, who revealed all this to <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> and who in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spired him with it, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.1, 2. The most infallible In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreter of his own Institutions, declared by these Signals and Types, and demonstrated by the frame of Ordinances, then given to the Church in these expressions, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.10. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.2, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17. The Veil ever covering the Holy of Holiest, but only in the day of Expiation, when it was drawn aside and that laid open.</ns0:note> this signifying, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 14.6.</ns0:note> the way into the holiest of all <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The true and ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry means to God's Presence in Heaven it self, which is on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly by Christ the great High-Priest, through whose Blood we can come to the Throne of his Grace there boldly, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10.19, 20, 21, 22. and by the perfect work of his Spirit on us, can enter with him into the Holy of Holiest in Heaven. This was not so plainly, clearly, fully, universally known as afterwards by the shedding of Christ's Blood, and the Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />velation of it in the Gospel to all the World. Christ was revealed to the <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> and all these Ceremonial Ordinances did hold him out, and by him only, the Saints under that Covenant-Administration got to Heaven, yet the manifesta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of it was obscure in comparison of what it is since.</ns0:note> was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">While the Mosaical Covenant-Administration was to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />continue, till the coming of Christ in the Flesh, and perfe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cting the work by his Death, for the space of near 1500 years was the true, right, and proper way for entring into Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, darkly, and obscurely, and typically revealed unto the Church, when by the Death of Christ the Vail of the Holy of Holiest was rent asunder, Heaven laid open to be seen, and entred into by all penitent believing Sinners through Christ, every day in their Duties, and then in their Persons; <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 27.51.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Which <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> a Figure for the time then pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Tabernacle in all its parts, and the whole Oecono<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />my of it was <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which signifieth the translation of a word or thing from its own natural signification, to signify another, which thing so signified by it, is commonly more excellent than it self, as the substance exceeds the shadow; equivalent it is to those terms of <ns0:hi>Types,</ns0:hi> Examples, <ns0:hi>Fi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gures</ns0:hi> of things to come; such are the Tabernacle and its Services, representations of things Spiritual and Divine, and very imperfect shadows of them, serving only for that In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fant state of the Church, and when its non-age was to ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pire by the coming of the Truths themselves, then were they to expire too, the time only when the Tabernacle-Administration was present and no longer.</ns0:note>, in which were offered both gifts and sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>In which</ns0:hi> Ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bernacle were performed Services to the great God, whose Tent it was, suitable to his Person, and agreeable to his Will, even Gifts and Sacrifices, as be<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ore described, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 5.1. and 8.3.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> that could not make him that did the service perfect <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">They were all impotent as to the restoring of a Sinner to God's favour by themselves, they could not re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />concile him to God, preserve Communion with him, nor bring them to happiness in him, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10.3, 4. no perfect justifying, sanctifying could be had by any of them though never so often repeated. They might do all to the Letter which God required, absolving the Worshipper as to the external part, but not at all according to the Conscience; or they could not take the guilt of Sin from the Consci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence as to themselves, but it would cry guilty still; neither could they remove the power of it, for it was under Bon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dage to it still; neither could they take away the fears and terrors of it, but left it shaking under them and un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quiet still, being abused by them as a Vail to keep them from Christ the true Priest and Sacrifice, when as Types and Shadows they should have led these Worshippers to him.</ns0:note>, as pertaining to the consci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:559" />10 <ns0:hi>Which stood</ns0:hi> only in meats and drinks <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Having shewn the typicalness, weakness of the Mosai<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cal Covenant-Administration, in respect of the Tabernacles, Services, and Ordinances, he closeth his Description of them in this Verse, by shewing their Carnality and Mortality. As they were external things, they could reach no further than the Flesh only, as appears by particular Instances, and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore could not quiet the Conscience, considered without Christ, nor justifie, sanctifie, or save the Sinner. For <ns0:hi>Meat and Drink-Offerings,</ns0:hi> and Meats clean and unclean, and Drinks prohibited by God, in which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> placed much of their Religion, which separate from what they signified, commend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed no Man unto God, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 8.8. As to Meats, see <ns0:hi>Lev. ch.</ns0:hi> 11. and <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 14.3, to 21. As to Drinks forbidden the Priests, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 10.9. and the <ns0:hi>Nazarites,</ns0:hi> Numb. 6.2, 3. The Jealousie-water, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 5.24. and the Paschal-cup, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 116.13. and Cup of Thankofferings; See <ns0:hi>Lev. ch.</ns0:hi> 1, and 2.</ns0:note>, and divers washing <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Which were many for the Priests in their Services, and for others in per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />forming theirs by them, some by sprinkling with Blood, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 29.20, 21. with Water, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 8.7. and 19.9, to 19. Some by washing at the brazen Laver, as the Priests, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 29.4. and 30.17, to 22. so the sprinkling of healed Leapers, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 14.4, to 9. and the Purification of the unclean. All these were of God's own instituting, but still reach no further than the Flesh or Body of the Sinner. See Verse 13.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Rites and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> carnal ordinances <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Other carnal Rites and Ceremonies, such as could not reach the Conscience, as they used them yet were to be used by them in obedience to God's Will, and to discriminate them from others, which were various in the Ceremonial Law. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>imposed,</ns0:hi> may agree with <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. <ns0:hi>Gifts imposed</ns0:hi>; or may have the whole Sentence for its Substantive, as, <ns0:hi>bring matters imposed or setled in Meats and Drinks.</ns0:hi> All these things were not the Inventions of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> but God's own Institutions injoyned by his own Authority on the Jewish Church to lead them by a regular Use of them to Life by Christ, but by their own Corruptions were made Burdens to them. The Divine Precept obliged them to an Observation of them, and to the serving God in, by, and through them.</ns0:note> imposed <ns0:hi>on them l,</ns0:hi> until the time <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">As they were outward bodily, and carnal things, so they were mortal; as to their Being and continuance enjoyned by God, they were <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>until,</ns0:hi> is a term setled and li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mited, and not indefinite, and its limit is a <ns0:hi>singular time,</ns0:hi> even that point of Time, wherein Christ having finished the Work of Redemption, ascended and sate down on the Right Hand of God, and powerfully thence breathed forth the Spirit of Infallibility on his Apostles, for guiding them in laying the Foundation of his Church, by preaching the Gospel throughout the World, and perfecting of it, and no other. This the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and others expected from the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> Joh. 4.25. in his time. All the New-Testament perfecting was by them, and therefore they give a charge against the least Al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teration of the Gospel, Truth, and Law, which they left as a Rule for ordering of Christ's Church to his last coming. See <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 28.20.</ns0:note> of refor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mation <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>of putting things to right</ns0:hi> by the Law, Rule, and Ordinance of Christ, the Work of this spe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cial point of Time. He the great Church-Reformer through<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly righteth things to God-ward, <ns0:hi>by removing and taking away</ns0:hi> what was faulty, not in it self, but by Man's abuse of it, even all the Mosaical Oeconomy and Church-frame, which carried Men about to God, by <ns0:hi>opening and making</ns0:hi> that to be seen with open Face, which was veiled and so mistaken, even the My<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stery of Christ hid from Ages, by <ns0:hi>manifesting and establishing</ns0:hi> that which was the Truth it self, instead of the Shadows that did but represent it, even that true <ns0:hi>Church-frame</ns0:hi> intended first by God, and now fully revealed and setled by his Son as a standing Rule and Pattern to all for ever; which un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />moveable Kingdom of his is described further <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 12.22, to 29.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 But <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The Spirit by this adversative <ns0:hi>But,</ns0:hi> opposeth and ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plieth the Truth to the Type, and brings in view the An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />titype, the Office, Tabernacle, Sacrifice and ministration of Christ, which vastly exceedeth the Mosaical one.</ns0:note> Christ being come <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.1.</ns0:note> an high priest of good things to come <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The High-Priest preferred, is no less Person than God the Son manifested in the Flesh, and anointed to his Office with the Holy Ghost and Power, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.38. In the fulness of time before the Antiquating and removing the former Order, was he exhibited and consecrated the true High-Priest, of which all the other were but Types, and bringing with him all those good things which were figured and promised under that Oeconomy, all Pardon, Reconciliation, Righteousness, Holiness, Adoption and glorious Salvation, which were under that dispensation to come, being present and ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hibited with, as effected by this High-Priest at his first coming, but to be compleated and perfected at his second, which is intimated <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 26.28.</ns0:note>, by a greater and more perfect <ns0:hi>q</ns0:hi> tabernacle, not made with hands <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">What is <ns0:hi>hand-wrought</ns0:hi> or made by Men, is at the best mouldring and decaying; but this was wrought by the Spirit of God himself; most ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cellent for the quality, permanency of the Materials and Work, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 2.22. Man had neither Power nor Skill to form, pollish, frame, or pitch this, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.2. <ns0:hi>Creation</ns0:hi>-work is God's Work, as to the Old and New Creation. Hands may frame and pitch the other, and pluck it up, but he that worketh, frameth, raiseth, createth, this is God, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.5. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.20.</ns0:note>, that is to say, not of this building:<ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The Anti-type of the Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />saical Sanctuary and Tabernacle, where there was the Holy Place, and the holy of Holiest, correspondent to, and figured out by these was the more <ns0:hi>Glorious Sanctuary</ns0:hi> of this High-Priest; he passeth through the Tabernacle of his Church on Earth, of which he is the Minister, as hath been cleared, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10. and <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.2. and so enters into the Heaven of Heavens, the Holiest of all, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24. where God sits on his Throne of Grace. <ns0:hi>Tabernacle</ns0:hi> here cannot signify the Body of Christ, for that is the Sacrifice that answereth to the legal ones offered in the Court, and without the Gate, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 13.11, 12, 13. and with the Blood of which he enters the Holy of Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liest as the High-Priest did, and he doth not pass through his Flesh there, but carrieth it with him. The Word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.14. May not only refer to the God-heads <ns0:hi>Tabernacling</ns0:hi> in Flesh; <ns0:hi>but that God the Son incarnate Taberna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cled in his Church</ns0:hi>; those with whom Christ dwelt while on Earth, for his Human Nature dwelt or had a Tabernacle in this World as well as his Deity; and this is such a Taber<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nacle where he in his whole Person and his Church may meet and communicate together: This Tabernacle is great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er than the Mosaical for quantity, as it refers to Earth the place, even the whole World, where his Church is disper<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed, beyond all comparison larger than its Type, which was a little limited and confined place, and <ns0:hi>more perfect</ns0:hi> than that which was only made of Boards, Gold, Silver, Brass, Silk, Linnen, Skins, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> This being a Spiritual Temple and Tent in which God will inhabit and dwell for ever, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.9, 16, 17. and 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.16. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 2.12.20, 21, 22. 1 <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> 2.5. It is far more glorious than that Tabernacle, <ns0:hi>Hag.</ns0:hi> 2.7, 8, 9.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Neither <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">From his Office and Sanctuary, he proceeds to clear up his Service; it was not about weak, typical vanishing Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices, the Blood of Goats or young Bulls, that he was concerned as the Aaronical Priests were, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.14, 15. opened before, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 7. And this annually on the expiatory-day, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.29, 34. which could not satisfie injured Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stice, nor expiate Sin, nor purge, nor quiet the Conscience of the Offender, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10.1, to 5.</ns0:note> by the blood of goats and calves: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 20.28. Rev. 1.5. and 5.9.</ns0:note> but by his own blood <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>But with his own pure, precious and unspotted Blood,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.19. Not a Drop or few Drops must go for it, then what dropped from his Body in his Agony, from his head pierced by Thorns, from his Back when Whip't, from his Hands and Feet when Nailed on the Cross might have done; but it must be <ns0:hi>his own Life, Blood,</ns0:hi> the Blood of the second <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> dying by it for the first, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.8, to 20. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.6, 8. And as it is the Blood of <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> that it may have value enough and worth; it must be the Blood of him who is God too, with his own Blood, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 20.28. This price surmounts all Treasures, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.51. and 10.11, 15. With this Blood of the <ns0:hi>Covenant</ns0:hi> he entred immediately upon the breathing out of his Soul on the Cross, (the Vail of the Temple being rent asunder, and room made for the great High-Priest to fulfil his Type) into the Holy of Holiest in Heaven, where never Angel came, nor any but himself, till his now piercing through, rending the Vail, and laying it open, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10.19. compare <ns0:hi>Isai.</ns0:hi> 57.15. and came with it to God's Throne of Justice there; and made the everlasting Atonement for Sin, and so turned it into a Throne of Grace, fulfilling his Type, and as the High-Priest did before the Sacrifice was burnt or consumed, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16. For the expiation of Sin was not deferred by Christ to his Ascension, 45 days after his Death; but was immediately on his giving up the Ghost by him performed, and in this fulfilled all righteousness, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 3.15. This is the <ns0:hi>onc<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> that he entred Heaven for expiation, satisfying the injured Justice of God by Sin, fulfilled the Law, and then publickly appeared at God's Throne, to shew all was com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pleat, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 23.43, 45, 46. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 19.30. <ns0:hi>This once</ns0:hi> he did that which the High-Priest did annually typifie, but could never accomplish <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

               <ns0:p n="22">22 And almost all things <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">All such things as are capable of <ns0:hi>purifying,</ns0:hi> and which were not to be so by the <ns0:hi>Water of Separation,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>by Fire,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 16.28. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 31.23. were ceremonial<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly purged by Blood.</ns0:note> are by the Law purged with blood: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 17.11.</ns0:note> without shedding of blood is no remission.<ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">And without the <ns0:hi>Death</ns0:hi> of some living Creature as a Sacrifice, and the <ns0:hi>Blood</ns0:hi> of it not only shed, but sprinkled, there could be neither legal Pardon of Giult, nor purging of Ceremonial filth. By this God sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> that without the <ns0:hi>Blood of Christ</ns0:hi> his Son, and the Testator of his Testament, shed as a Sacrifice, to pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chase and procure both remission and the Spirit, there could be neither pardon of the guilt of Sin, and removal of the punishment, nor purging the filth, or renewing the nature of the Sinner, his Blood being the inestimable price purchasing both for them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:hi>It was</ns0:hi> necessary therefore <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This conclusion the Spirit draweth from the antecedent, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18. proved in the following Verses, therefore is it here rehearsed the illative Particle <ns0:hi>therefore,</ns0:hi> is but to summ up the use of Blood about the first Tabernacle, and that Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stament-dispensation. It is positively <ns0:hi>necessary</ns0:hi> by the Will of God, expressively enjoining them, to point out better, and that there might be an agreement of the Type with the Truth.</ns0:note>, that the pat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terns of the things in the Heaven <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The Tabernacles in all their parts, the Book of the Covenant, Vessels, Services, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Being Types, Signs, Examples, Shadows of things in Heaven, must be ceremo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nially purged and separated from common use to Divine, by those external, ritual sprinkling and lustrations, especi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally with <ns0:hi>Beasts Blood,</ns0:hi> mystically representing better Blood and Purifications of persons and things than these.</ns0:note> should be purified with these, but the heavenly <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">But things more excellent and glorious than earthly ones, the Gospel-Tabernacle in its parts, Testament, and Services, about which Christ ministreth, which are Heavenly for their de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cent, agreeableness with, and tendency to it; they are spiritual and it corruptible, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11, 12. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.2. and 12.22. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 4.26. <ns0:hi>Revel.</ns0:hi> 21. are to be dedicated, set apart, put in force, and sanctified to God by the one Sacrifice of Christ, of more value, worth, and virtue than all the legal Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fices together. It is expressed <ns0:hi>plurally,</ns0:hi> to answer the op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posite term, and to set out its excellency, being far above all others; the Blood of it being that of God by personal union, and which is only efficacious for eternal good, and available with him; so ought it to be esteemed as it was in Truth, and not quarrelled with by these <ns0:hi>Hebrews.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> things themselves with better sacrifices than these.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 For Christ is not entred <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> shews this to be a rational proof of the transcen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dency of Christ's Death and Sacrifice; and this he demon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strates from the <ns0:hi>place of his Ministry,</ns0:hi> far exceeding that of his Type. The Gospel-High-Priest did not like <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter with his Blood into the Holy of Holiest of an earthly Tabernacle, frail and moveable, and appear before the Mer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cy-Seat on the Ark there, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9.</ns0:note> into holy pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces made with hands, <ns0:hi>which are</ns0:hi> the figures <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">All these were but like, and correspondent figures, and resemblances of the true, holy, and glorious place of God's residence.</ns0:note> of the true, but into heaven <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">But he, as our High-Priest, did enter with his Atoning-Blood; after the Sacrificing of himself on the Cross, into the Heaven of Heavens, and approached the Throne of Justice, and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pitiated it, making it a Mercy-Seat and true Throne of Grace unto penitent, believing Sinners; and then perfected the work of Propitiation and Redemption: Afterwards at his triumphant Ascension he entred in his whole person im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mortal, and laid open a way for our entring there.</ns0:note> it self, now to appear <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Where he now appears as our Advocating Mediator, pleading his Merit for the remission of our Sins, and rendring of God's face smiling on, and favouring his Clients, which was ter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rifying and afrighting guilty <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> before. See <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 7.25. and 10.19. and <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.34. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.1, 2. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 5.6. Here he represents our persons to God's Face, fitting in the mean while us beneath for our seeing him face to face, and being blessed in the enjoyment of that prospect for ever.</ns0:note> in the presence of God for u<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

               <ns0:p n="25">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:561" />25 Nor <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The excellency of Christ's Sacrifice beyond the <ns0:hi>Aaro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nical,</ns0:hi> is argued here from its singularity; it needs no re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />petition, as their multiplied Sacrifices did. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> introdu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cing it, is but inferring this excellency of Christ's Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice, by denying in it that weakness which was annexed to the legal ones; there was no need that he should die yearly, to fulfil the Type of the often yearly Sacrifices of the Legal High-Priest, who entred with the Blood of Bulls and Goats, strange Blood to him, and not his own, into the Holy of Holiest in the Tabernacle, and entred so eve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry year once to shew the vertue of his Sacrifice to be only signal, typical, and passing, to make room for a bet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter, that single individual one of Christ, in respect of Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice and Oblation.</ns0:note> yet that he should offer himself often, as <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 7.</ns0:note> the high-priest entreth into the Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly place every year with the blood of o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 For then <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, The consequent is drawn <ns0:hi>ab impossibili</ns0:hi>; if he had often offered himself, he must have often suffered, but he could not suffer often. For where there was Offering, there must be a Sacrifice, and so Suffering. Now that Christ should do so in his own Person, was impossible and absurd, for God to have put his Son on suffering so cruel a Death so often,</ns0:note> must he often have suffered since <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">From the Fall of <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> at the be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning of the World, ever since Sin needed a Sacrifice: but his once suffering as a Sacrifice for it, was of Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Virtue in God's purpose, answering and satisfying God's Justice; one Death of the second <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> for the Sin and Penalty of the first; in the efficacy and vertue of his Death which was everlasting. The often and annual Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crificing of the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priests, and entring of the Holy of Holiest with the Blood of Beasts, was to shew the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> their Weakness, and to instruct them in, and lead them to this one Sacrifice once to be offered, of eternal Avail, as is subjoyned.</ns0:note> the foundation of the world: But now <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">But Christ the Gospel-High-Priest was not on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly God-Man, manifested to be so, and exhibited as such an Officer by his Work, but was manifested to be such by Promise, and in Types and Figures from <ns0:hi>Adam's</ns0:hi> Fall; but now shewed it clearly in his Suffering-work, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 3.16. The days of Christ's Ministry on Earth under the fourth Monarchy, called the last Days and Times, 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.18. The <ns0:hi>end of the World,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.11. <ns0:hi>The fulness of time,</ns0:hi> Gal. 4.4. God's set and best time for his Appearance, and it was but once that he appeared in these days, performing this Work.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 12.</ns0:note> once in <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Eph. 1.10.</ns0:note> the end of the world hath he <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Then he sacrificed himself, offered up his Blood to God within the Vail, taking away by his own Blood, which God required, the Guilt, Stain and Power of all Sin, justifying Believers from any Condemnation by it, by what he did and suffered in their stead for their good, who flie from it for refuge to him, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53. <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.24. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 7.24, 25. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.5.</ns0:note> ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peared to put away sin by the sacrifice of him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And as it is appointed <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The Proof of the necessity of Christ's suffering Death but once, is introduced in this Verse by the Conjunction <ns0:hi>And.</ns0:hi> It was according to God's decreed and published Statute of Mens but once dying; for God the Supreme Lord, Governour and Judge of them, set, constituted, and appointed by an unalterable and irrevocable Decree, as Law-giver, and Sen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tence, as Judge to all of the sinful Humane Race, the corrupt Seed of Apostate <ns0:hi>Adam,</ns0:hi> their grand Representative, whom God threatned with this Penalty upon his sinning and transgressing his Law, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 2.17. which Sentence was de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nounced upon him, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.19. comp. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.12, 14. and 6.23. This Sentence was but <ns0:hi>once</ns0:hi> to be undergone by him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self and all his sinful Off-spring, and by their Surety, and no more; so that the second <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> needed but once to die by this Statute. No Man can keep himself from this, it being the general Rule of God's proceeding with all Persons. The Supreme <ns0:hi>Legislator</ns0:hi> may make what Exception and <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viso</ns0:hi>'s to his Law he pleaseth. Those that were translated by him, did suffer a Change proportionable to Death, as <ns0:hi>Enoch,</ns0:hi> ch. 11.5. <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 5.24. and <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> 2 King. 2.11, 12. and those that shall be changed at Christ's coming, must un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dergoe the like, as 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.51, to 55. and 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 4.17. Those that were raised from Death by Christ, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> &c. God might glorifie his Name by reiterating it; but whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther they did die again, is not certain. This is to be the gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral setled Law and Rule of God.</ns0:note> unto men once to die, but after this the judgment <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">In order, after Souls by Death are separated from their Bodies, they come <ns0:hi>to Iudg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment</ns0:hi>: And thus every particular one is handed over by Death to the Bar of God, the great Judge, and so is dispatched by his Sentence to its particular State and Place with its respe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctive People, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 14.12. At the great and general Assize, the Day of Judgment, shall the General and Universal One take place, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 17.31. when all Sinners in their entire Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons, Bodies and Souls united, shall be adjudged to their final, unalterable and eternal State, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 14.10. and 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.10. <ns0:hi>Iude v.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 20.11, to 15.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
